# blender-lighting-material-planner

Purpose: Build detailed lighting and material direction with portability and caveat handling for Blender/web-3D outputs.

Create a high-quality, practical lighting/material plan that balances visual intent and web portability constraints.

Metadata: Category `scene-planners` | Role `lighting-rig-and-lookdev-deep-planner` | Tier `L0` | Runtime default `Not Run` | Artifact default `Not Produced` | Mutation `downgrade_only`

## When to use & trigger cues
- look-development strategy is needed
- lighting/material choices drive scene mood
- web/GLB portability caveats must be explicit
- Trigger phrases: "plan lighting and materials", "design cyberpunk lookdev", "define PBR and reflection strategy"

## When not to use (delegation boundaries)
- to claim final rendered quality or executed results → use `blender-composition-camera-planner` (`references/skill-blender-composition-camera-planner.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to blender-composition-camera-planner)
- to skip composition/camera context from blender-composition-camera-planner → use `blender-composition-camera-planner` (`references/skill-blender-composition-camera-planner.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to blender-composition-camera-planner)
- to validate existing lighting or materials → use `lighting-quality-checker` (`references/skill-lighting-quality-checker.md`; use lighting-quality-checker and material-quality-checker)
- to decide render engines (cycles-vs-eevee-decision), color management (color-management-decision), or file formats (output-format-decision) → use `color-management-decision` (`references/skill-color-management-decision.md`; output-format-decision)
- to execute Blender or generate Python scripts → use `color-management-decision` (`references/skill-color-management-decision.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to color-management-decision)

## Input & output contract
- Required input `domain_scene_plan` (`object`): Upstream scene layout and subject surface description
- Required input `camera_framing_plan` (`object`): Locked camera angles and hero silhouette requirements from blender-composition-camera-planner
- Optional input `target_render_engine_hint` (`string`): Preferred engine (Cycles, Eevee, or WebGL/GLB PBR export target)
- Output contract: `key_fill_rim_lighting_plan`, `pbr_material_and_roughness_spec`, `hdri_and_reflection_strategy` (Runtime status: `Not Run`, Artifact status: `Not Produced`, `downgrade_only`).

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- Runtime boundary: This is a planning-only skill: no Blender execution, no Python, and no artifact generation. Runtime status always remains `Not Run` and artifact status always remains `Not Produced` (truth states are downgrade-only, never upgrade). If referencing Eevee engine tokens from upstream `cycles-vs-eevee-decision`, use `BLENDER_EEVEE` on Blender 4.0–4.1 and 5.x, and `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` only for 4.2–4.x — never present Eevee Next as the current name.
- shader/runtime implementation code
- rendered quality claims without evidence
